title: Pilgrimage of the Sun Guard - a journaling / solo-RPG from Amanda P.
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EFc5_Nct8wE

Daniel (@dungeondive) plays through *Pilgrimage of the Sun Guard*, a short journaling solo RPG by Amanda P., and is upfront that it is almost entirely a creative-writing exercise rather than a crunchy adventure game. He likens it to a journaling take on *Call to Adventure*, and notes its acknowledged influences include *Thousand Year Old Vampire*, *Dark Souls* and *The Oregon Trail*.

You play one of the last members of a fading solar order, summoned to ride the ancient roads. The loop is simple: travel to a location, spend time, roll 2d6 for a prompt, write, and spend or regain the resources of **might, honour, guile and time**, earning deeds as you go. Two omens drawn at departure let you take a prompt for free if you weave them in.

Most of the video walks through his own pilgrim, Astrid — a romantic haunted by prisoners he once let die — across desert, shadowy pines, river valley and frost cliffs. He hangs his father's compass on a stag king's antlers, befriends a graveyard beast, loses a joust with dignity, and trades memories to a weirdling.

Daniel's verdict: a good morning-coffee exercise for the imagination and for building characters to carry into other games, though he sometimes wishes these were a little more game.

----

Do you use journaling games purely for their own sake, or as a workshop for characters and settings you later take into other systems?
